title: SPID: Distilled Protein Backbone Generation
abstract: arXiv:2510.03095v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Diffusion- and flow-based generative models have recently demonstrated strong performance in protein backbone generation tasks, offering unprecedented capabilities for de novo protein design. However, despite their generation quality, these models are constrained by slow sampling, often requiring hundreds of iterative steps. This computational bottleneck limits their practical utility in large-scale protein discovery, where thousands to millions of candidate structures are needed. To address this challenge, we explore the techniques of score distillation, which has shown great success in reducing the number of sampling steps in the vision domain while maintaining high generation quality. However, a straightforward adaptation of these methods results in unacceptably low designability. We introduce Score Protein identity Distillation (SPID), which resolves this incompatibility by combining few-step generation with inference-time noise

translated_abstract: 基于扩散模型和流模型的生成式方法最近在蛋白质主链生成任务中展现出卓越性能，为从头蛋白质设计提供了前所未有的能力。然而，尽管这些模型生成质量很高，但它们受到采样速度缓慢的制约，通常需要数百次迭代步骤。这一计算瓶颈限制了它们在大规模蛋白质发现中的实际应用，因为大规模蛋白质发现需要数千到数百万个候选结构。为了应对这一挑战，我们探索了分数蒸馏技术，该技术在视觉领域已成功地在保持高生成质量的同时大幅减少采样步骤数量。然而，将这些方法直接迁移到蛋白质生成中会导致设计性低到不可接受的程度。我们提出了分数蛋白质恒等蒸馏，通过将少步生成与推理时噪声相结合，解决了这一不兼容性问题。
tldr: 提出SPID方法，将视觉领域的分数蒸馏技术成功迁移到蛋白质主链生成中，通过结合少步生成与推理时噪声策略，解决了直接蒸馏导致设计性过低的问题，实现了快速高质量的蛋白质主链生成。
en_tdlr: SPID adapts score distillation to protein backbone generation by combining few-step generation with inference-time noise techniques, resolving the low designability issue of naive distillation and enabling fast, high-quality de novo protein design.
